project: Abbott Cyber Consulting — GRC Security Scorecard
description: Feature backlog for the Security Scorecard / GRC Platform MVP. Items are ordered by build phase. Mark done: true when a feature is built and approved.
build_approach: Artifact-first MVP built in Claude. Each session picks the next open section, builds it as an interactive artifact, user approves, item marked done.

sections.title: Core Concept
sections.description: Foundational platform capabilities — the spine everything else attaches to.

items.text: Security posture scoring for organisations / clients
Phase 1: Survey-based input (quick start, no tooling required)
Phase 2: Ingest vuln scan results (Nessus, Qualys, etc.)
Phase 3: Pen test findings integration
Unified score across all data sources

sections.title: Platform Dashboard Shell

items.text: Sidebar navigation with grouped modules (Assessments, Risk Management, Compliance, Exercises, Reporting)
Org switcher dropdown: Platform / Grandfather / Father / Child four-tier selector with tier-scoped visibility
items.notes: Session 23b: buildOrgDropdown() rewritten to render a parent→child tree instead of flat tier-labelled sections. renderNode() recurses from root orgs (no parent or parent outside visible set) through children, adding 14px indent per depth level and muted '—' dash prefixes. Tier-coloured avatars still indicate level. Roots sorted by TIER_ORDER then name; children sorted alphabetically.

items.text: Dashboard home: org tier card, assessments run, avg posture score, quick links

Panels are role-scoped via hasModuleAccess() — users with no module access see a 'Limited access' message; users with partial access see only their permitted panels. Quick links strip also filtered by module access. _homeAssessmentsChicklet(), _homeRiskChicklet(), _homeAiChicklet() are the three panel renderers. Session 23e: original redesign — two-column layout, live modules removed, sub-orgs removed, drawHomeCharts() draws sparklines + radar.

New fields needed: approx_device_count, approx_user_count (separate from employee_count_band), primary_msp. PATCH_019 needed for new columns.

items.text: Module routing: live modules open inline, unbuilt modules show phase/coming-soon card
Score dot indicators on sidebar nav items (green/amber/red based on latest score)
Topbar breadcrumb and active org pill

items.notes: Built. 153 safeguards across 18 control groups, IG1/IG2/IG3 tiering, full assessment form with Yes/Partial/No/NA answers, per-safeguard comments, Quick Check (47 questions), POAM, and Executive Report.

items.text: Insurance Readiness Assessment: dual-weighted scoring (security + insurance premium impact)
Accordion-style survey panels per category, inline scoring
Save & record score: each submission appends to org assessment history
Trend line chart: score history per module per org
Premium savings estimator: gap-based insurance cost reduction estimates

items.notes: Session 24: renderInsurance() now routes to renderInsuranceDashboard() or renderInsuranceForm() via insState.view. Dashboard has navy score-hero (score, Sec%, Ins%, run count), trend chart, history table with Latest badge and Edit button, savings panel from latest run. insOpenAssessment(origIdx) loads past run into form. insBackToDashboard() returns to dashboard. insSave() saves conducted_by + assessed_at and reloads history before switching view. insState in config.js and selectOrg() in app.js updated; duplicateAssessment() in home.js updated to set view:form. sections.title: Technology Stack Survey

items.notes: 10 categories, 41 questions delivered. Y/N/NA/Partial answer model with inline partial-detail capture. tool_category machine tag on every question for MSP catalog match. SUPABASE_PATCH_002.sql adds techstack_responses table.

items.text: Per-tool selection auto-maps to CIS Controls, NIST CSF, and Insurance Readiness scoring
items.notes: Each question carries mappings.cis (with IG tier), mappings.nist (CSF 2.0 IDs), mappings.insurance (impact rating + note). Rendered as individually-clickable chip-lets under each question.

items.text: Technical maturity score: pre-populated baseline before manual survey questions are answered
items.notes: Overall + per-category maturity computed live (Yes=1, Partial=0.5, No=0, NA=excluded). Snapshot writes to assessments table with module='techstack' on save, feeding the dashboard score dot. Session 27: Edit button added to each history row — tsEditSnapshot(id) looks up run in orgAssessments, pre-fills date/conductedBy, sets tsState.editId, opens form. tsSaveAllResponses() PATCHes existing record (sb.updateAssessment) when editId is set, then clears it. Form subtitle and save button text reflect edit vs new mode. tsNavToDashboard() clears editId.

items.text: Gap view: which framework controls have no tool coverage
items.notes: Follow-up: dedicated view that inverts the mapping — shows CIS/NIST controls grouped by 'No' or unanswered tech stack questions.

items.text: Tool stack summary card: exportable for client-facing technology posture review
items.notes: Export JSON button delivers full snapshot including tool_category, question_type, derive_strategy tags for downstream MSP catalog matching and framework auto-scoping.

items.text: Optional category toggles (Cloud Security Posture, Application Security) — show only when client has cloud / SaaS scope
Move questions from JS const into Supabase techstack_questions table so MSPs can manage their own question sets without code deploys
MSP tool catalog (msp_tools table) + join logic to classify each client answer as sell / upgrade / replace opportunity
Framework auto-scoping: tech stack answers pre-populate CIS / NIST / Insurance survey questions via derive_strategy
items.notes: Session 25: Pull model — 'From Tech Stack' button appears on new assessments only (not edits). js/prefill.js contains tsDeriveCIS() (walks TS_CATS mappings.cis to derive yes/partial/no per safeguard; better answer wins when multiple TS questions map to same safeguard) and tsDeriveInsurance() (14-entry static map to Insurance question IDs; maps TS yes/partial/no to closest option score via option index). tsEnsureLoaded() silently loads TS from Supabase if not yet in memory. insPrefillFromTS() and cisPrefillFromTS() fill only unanswered questions (never overwrites). insState.fromNew=true set in insNew(); CIS button gated on !cisState.editId. q12 (IR Plan documented) intentionally excluded — no TS proxy for a written plan.

sections.title: CIS Controls v8 — Enhancements
sections.description: Extensions to the CIS Controls assessment module: per-safeguard evidence capture, auditor comments, and deeper reporting.

items.text: Per-safeguard assessor comments: free-text note field per safeguard in the assessment form, persisted in the answers jsonb or a dedicated table. Display inline in form and read-only in assessment detail view.
items.notes: Implemented. 💬 Comment button toggles inline textarea per safeguard. Notes saved to cis_safeguard_notes table (PATCH_007). Evidence columns (evidence_url, evidence_filename) added to same table for Phase 2.

items.text: Per-safeguard evidence upload: file attachment (PDF, screenshot, doc) linked to a safeguard and an assessment run. Store in Supabase Storage; show filename + download link in form and detail view. New SQL patch required.

CIS Quick Check: 47 plain-language questions across all 18 CIS control groups. No evidence required. Fast posture read for client intake. Lives inside the CIS module dashboard. Saves to assessments table as module=cis_quick.
items.notes: Built. renderCISQuick() with score-so-far hero, progress bar, per-control group sections. cisSaveQuick() / cisOpenQuickAssessment() / cisDeleteQuickAssessment(). Dashboard shows Quick Check history card below full assessment history.

items.text: CIS POAM (Plan of Action & Milestones): per-assessment gap report with Assigned To, Target Date, Risk Decision (Remediate/Accept/Transfer), Rationale, Status columns. Excel export with logo placeholder row. POAM button on each assessment history row.
items.notes: Built. cis_poam_items table (PATCH_008). renderCISPoam(), cisOpenPoam(), cisSavePoam(), cisExportPoam(). Logo row placeholder in Excel export (row 1) — full logo upload is backlogged.

items.text: CIS control scope descriptions in Gap Report and POAM — CIS_CONTROL_SCOPE descriptions are shown in the assessment accordion (session 27) but not yet in cisOpenGapReport() or renderCISPoam(). Add scope as a sub-line under each control group header in both views.

CIS POAM remediation suggestions — add a '💡 Suggested Action' block to each safeguard row in the CIS POAM, giving practitioners specific implementation guidance rather than just a gap reference. Same pattern as AI Unified POAM (AI_REMEDIATION lookup). Requires a CIS_REMEDIATION object or per-safeguard field added to CIS_SAFEGUARDS.
Client logo upload for POAM and report exports: allow logo upload in Organisation Manager, stored in Supabase Storage, embedded in Excel/PDF exports at top of document.
CIS assessment PDF/Excel export: produce a formatted report card showing score, IG progress, per-control summary, and gap list — branded Abbott Cyber.
items.notes: Session 28: Excel export (cisExportExcel) now includes Column H 'Comment' populated with existing assessor notes; import (cisParseImportFile + cisImportSave) reads Column H back and saves to cis_safeguard_notes. Word exec report (cisExportReportWord) now embeds radar chart + dot/line trend chart as inline PNG images captured from cisReportRadar and cisReportTrend canvases, plus a page-break section with the full 18-control/153-safeguard detail listing showing each safeguard ID, IG tier, answer (colour-coded), title and description.

items.text: CIS exec report Print / Save as PDF button: add a 'Print' button on the exec report view that calls window.print() with @media print CSS to hide nav/buttons and produce a clean client-presentable PDF directly from the browser, without needing to open the Word download.

CIS Executive Report: per-assessment report view with gauge/speedometer chart, answer distribution donut, score trend line, IG tier progress bars, control group coverage bars, top gaps table, and executive commentary section with 'Generate AI Prompt' button to produce AI-written narrative via Claude.
items.notes: Built. cisOpenReport() opens report view, renderCISReport() renders full layout. cisDrawGauge(), cisDrawDonut(), cisDrawReportTrend() draw Canvas charts. cisGenerateReportPrompt() copies data-rich prompt to clipboard. cisSaveCommentary() persists commentary to assessment answers._exec_commentary via PATCH. Session 8 overhaul: added cisDrawRadar() 18-spoke canvas radar; accordion redesigned with CIS_REPORT_LAYERS. Session 28: cisDrawReportTrend() = stacked IG1/IG2/IG3 bar chart (in-browser only). cisDrawTrendLine() = new dot/line trend chart for Word export only (drawn off-screen). cisCaptureHeader() helper prevents date/assessor reverting on answer clicks. cisGenerateReportPrompt() rewritten with explicit no-markdown formatting rules. Session 29: cisExportReportWord() fully restructured — new section order: Executive Summary → Overall Score (SVG gauge dial) → Radar → IG Progress (in-scope tiers only) → Score Trend (line chart) → Top 10 Priority Gaps → Full Assessment page-break (IG-scoped safeguards only). Commentary parsed from ---CONTROLS---/---TREND---/---GAPS--- delimiters. cisDrawReportTrend() rewritten as proper stacked bar: IG1 bottom (green), IG2 middle (blue), IG3 top (purple); each zone fills from bottom by tier score%; score % label inside each zone; overall score label above bar; now draws with 1+ runs. fmtCommentary() rewritten line-by-line: KEY FINDINGS → navy sub-heading + bullet table (• column); PRIORITY RECOMMENDATIONS → navy sub-heading + numbered navy-cell table (1/2/3); handles AI output with single or double \n, with or without • characters. Radar and trend now drawn fresh on off-screen canvases at export time (not captured from in-page canvas which could be stale). Session 30: Gauge replaced SVG (unreliable in Word) with canvas→PNG — full red→orange→amber→lime→green spectrum track, needle, hub circle. Report title now dynamic: 'CIS IG2 Assessment — Executive Report'. IG progress table: N/A column added, gap count excludes N/A, score denominator excludes N/A. AI prompt: 80% advancement threshold logic — ≥80% recommends advancing to next IG; <80% recommends consolidating; exec summary instructed to close with next-year scope recommendation. JS script tags: ?v=20260618b cache-bust added to all modules.

items.text: CIS assessment form: IG filter bar (All / IG1 / IG2 / IG3) to narrow visible safeguards by implementation group tier.
items.notes: Session 30. cisSetIgFilter(val) updates cisState.igFilter and re-renders. Filter bar rendered above control panels in renderCISForm(). filterN applied to scopedSfs — controls with zero matching safeguards hidden entirely. Header stats remain based on full goal scope. Panel subtitle shows 'showing IGx only' when filter active.

items.text: CIS gap report: dedicated view listing all unanswered or 'No' safeguards for the selected IG goal, sorted by control group, with recommended remediation priority.
items.notes: Built. cisOpenGapReport(idx) opens gap view; renderCISGapReport() renders grouped-by-control table with priority badges (Critical/High/Medium/Low derived from IG tier × answer status). cisGapPriority() matrix. cisGapCopyPrompt() copies a remediation roadmap prompt for Claude. 🔍 Gaps button added to each assessment row in the dashboard. Includes summary stat chips and priority legend.

sections.title: Authentication & User Management
sections.description: Supabase Auth email/password login, session management, role-based access control, and user management UI.

items.text: Supabase Auth email/password login screen — gates entire app before init(). Session token stored in sessionStorage. Token refresh on expiry.
items.notes: js/auth.js: authBootstrap(), authSignIn(), authSignOut(), loginSubmit(), renderLoginScreen(). sbFetch updated to use session token in Authorization header. startApp() replaces init() as entry point.

items.text: 4-role model: platform_admin, org_admin, analyst, viewer. Visibility scoping per role. Viewer role is read-only (write ops blocked at sbFetch level).
items.notes: visibleOrgs() updated to be auth-aware. viewOnlyBanner() shown on assessment modules. sbFetch blocks POST/PATCH/DELETE for viewer role. adminOnly flag on User Management nav item.

items.text: User Management module — list, create, edit, delete users. Multi-org access assignment for analyst/viewer. user_org_access junction table.
items.notes: js/users.js: renderUserManagement(), openCreateUserModal(), openEditUserModal(). Auth account created via /auth/v1/signup (anon key). SUPABASE_PATCH_009.sql adds auth_id to users, user_org_access table, authenticated RLS policies.

items.text: Remove anon RLS policies — tighten to authenticated-only once auth is confirmed stable.
items.notes: PATCH_010 pending. Current state: both anon and authenticated policies active.

items.text: First-run setup screen — allow platform admin account creation from login screen when no platform_admin users exist, eliminating need for Supabase dashboard bootstrap.
Audit log — cross-module activity tracking with 7/30/90 day filter. Covers user, assessment, TPRA, org, and POAM events. Displayed as a tab in User Management.
items.notes: SUPABASE_PATCH_011.sql: audit_log table (org_id, actor_name, actor_email, event_type, target_type, target_name, details jsonb, created_at). js/supabase.js: sb.auditLog.insert(), sb.auditLog.getRecent(), global auditLog() fire-and-forget helper. js/users.js: Audit Log tab with renderAuditShell(), auditTabLoad(), setAuditDays(). Audit calls wired in users.js (create/edit/delete), cis.js (save/update/POAM/delete), insurance.js (save), tpra.js (publish/delete), orgs.js (create/update/delete).

items.text: Wire auditLog() into Technology Stack save — currently the only module without an audit call.
Export audit log to CSV — allow platform admins to download the filtered audit log as a spreadsheet.
Verify RLS UPDATE policy on organisation_profiles — CIS IG goal upsert was returning 409 duplicate key error.
items.notes: Session 19: Root cause was sb.profiles.upsert() calling POST without specifying the conflict column — PostgREST defaulted to PK (id) but id was not in the payload, so the ON CONFLICT clause never fired and it tried to INSERT a duplicate org_id. Fixed by adding ?on_conflict=org_id to the URL in supabase.js. No SQL patch required.

items.text: Module-level access control — add module_access jsonb column to users table (PATCH_012); restrict nav group visibility per analyst/viewer based on assigned modules (AI Readiness, Assessments, Risk & Vendors, Exercises, Reports). platform_admin and org_admin always see all. UI reads module_access in buildNav() to filter groups.
items.notes: SUPABASE_PATCH_012.sql adds module_access jsonb to users. js/app.js: _GROUP_MODULE map, hasModuleAccess(groupId) — only platform_admin bypasses unconditionally; all other roles (including org_admin) are gated by module_access jsonb. NULL = full access (existing users unaffected). buildNav() calls hasModuleAccess() per group. js/users.js: Module Access checkboxes always visible in create/edit modals — active for all roles except platform_admin (greyed/disabled for platform_admin only). submitCreateUser/submitEditUser save module_access for role !== 'platform_admin'. Org access (user_org_access) still only saved for analyst/viewer. Run PATCH_012 in Supabase SQL Editor to activate.

items.text: View As User — platform_admin can impersonate any user to preview their exact nav, org scope, and module access. Amber banner shows who is being viewed. All writes disabled in preview mode. Exit returns to own account.
items.notes: js/config.js: viewAsState global + _orgScopeForRole() helper refactors visibleOrgs(). js/auth.js: isAdmin/isViewOnly check viewAsState first; isPlatformAdmin() always uses real role. js/supabase.js: writes blocked when viewAsState active. js/app.js: viewAsUser(userId), exitViewAs(), updateViewAsBanner(). hasModuleAccess() checks viewAsState. js/users.js: '👁 View As' button per user row (platform_admin only, not in view-as mode). index.html: #viewAsBanner div between topbar and content. css/core.css: .view-as-banner amber styles. Session 15b fixes: renderUserMenu() now shows viewed user name/role/avatar (amber) in view-as mode; viewAsUser()/exitViewAs() call updateOrgUI() + re-render user chip. activeNavSection default changed to null (no section pre-opened). Module Access always visible in user modals — greyed/disabled for admin roles with explanatory note, active for analyst/viewer.

items.text: Delete user now removes Supabase Auth account — requires SB_SERVICE_KEY in js/supabase.js (service role key from Supabase Dashboard → Settings → API). Graceful fallback if key not set.
items.notes: js/supabase.js: SB_SERVICE_KEY constant. js/auth.js: authAdminDeleteUser(authId) calls DELETE /auth/v1/admin/users/{id} with service role key. js/users.js: deleteUser() retrieves auth_id from userMgmtState, calls authAdminDeleteUser after app record deleted. Soft failure: if auth delete fails, shows warning toast and audit logs the failure rather than crashing. 404 from auth treated as success. Session 15b: service role key populated in SB_SERVICE_KEY.

items.text: Move SB_SERVICE_KEY out of client-side code before any hosting or deployment — service role key bypasses all RLS and must never be in a publicly accessible file. Options: Supabase Edge Function for auth-admin operations, or a thin server-side proxy. Currently safe as a local-only tool but must be resolved before SaaS/white-label.

sections.title: Third-Party Risk Assessment (TPRA)
sections.description: Vendor risk assessment module. 5-step guided wizard to assess vendors by data sensitivity and risk signals, producing a tiered risk rating and recommendations.

items.text: Vendor intake: name, product, website, assessor, data categories with sensitivity labels, jurisdiction, data residency, provided docs
Vendor profile: company intelligence fields (legal entity, size, HQ, certifications, breach history, etc.) with Verified / Inferred / Unknown confidence labels
Risk findings: area, severity (Critical–Info), confidence, applies-to, detail, recommendation; vendor follow-up items list
Auto-suggested risk tier: data sensitivity × vendor signals matrix → Critical / High / Moderate / Low with manual override and rationale field
Review & publish: assessment summary, save as draft, complete, edit, delete from list
Supabase persistence: full CRUD against vendor_assessments table (PATCH_005)
items.notes: Code complete. WARNING: vendor_assessments table is missing from the live DB — sql/SUPABASE_PATCH_005.sql needs to be re-run in the Supabase SQL Editor to restore it before TPRA saves will work.

items.text: Copy report prompt for Claude: pre-filled prompt to generate a .docx vendor risk report
Push High/Critical findings to Risk Register as Third-Party risk entries on completion
items.notes: Checkbox UI is already in place on Step 5. Blocked by Risk Register module (Phase 2). Wire up once risk_register_core is built.

items.text: Native PDF export of completed vendor risk assessment (Abbott Cyber branded)
Vendor register: filter and sort assessment list by tier, status, data sensitivity, or assessor

Technical OSINT Layer: structured sub-step for active public-surface checks — port/TLS exposure (Shodan/Censys), certificate hygiene (crt.sh), email security records (SPF/DKIM/DMARC DNS lookup), and credential leak history (HIBP). Makes technical findings independently defensible rather than reliant on vendor self-reporting.

Structured CVE Pass: dedicated NVD/CVE search step against the product name, GitHub security advisories, and vendor changelog. Current skill catches CVEs opportunistically; a structured pass catches quieter vulnerabilities.
Risk Rating Framework Anchor: add one methodology note anchoring the impact/likelihood matrix to NIST SP 800-30. No workflow change — purely a defensibility and audit-readiness addition.

Data Taxonomy Expansion: add CUI, ITAR-controlled technical data, IP/source code, and OT/SCADA to the default data category checklist. Expands TAM to CMMC clients, defense-adjacent, and industrial verticals. ITAR and Canadian frameworks are currently absent from all competing platforms.

Periodic Reassessment Tracking: add a next-review date field and documented re-trigger conditions (ownership change, breach disclosure, major version release) to the report output. Converts a point-in-time artifact into a recurring program item.

sections.title: Org Hierarchy — Grandfather / Father / Child Model
sections.description: Three-tier multi-tenancy model supporting both MSP and franchise organisational structures.

items.text: Define three-tier org model: Grandfather (MSP/Franchisor) → Father (Region/Group) → Child (Site/Client)
Grandfather tenant: full visibility across all Father and Child orgs
Father tenant: manages and reports across its own Child orgs only
Child tenant: self-contained org with own data, assessments, and users
Role-based access control enforced at each tier (no cross-tenant data leakage)
items.notes: App-level done: auth roles (platform_admin/org_admin/analyst/viewer) gate visibility via visibleOrgs() and the org switcher. DB-level RLS still has open anon policies alongside authenticated ones — full per-org enforcement at DB layer is PATCH_010 (auth4 in backlog).

items.text: MSP use case: Grandfather = MSP, Father = MSP client group or vertical, Child = end client
Franchise use case: Grandfather = Franchisor HQ, Father = Regional operator, Child = individual location
Child orgs can be onboarded by Father or Grandfather with templated baseline configs
Grandfather can push policy baselines and compliance frameworks down to all tiers
Each tier can have its own branding (white-label support for MSP resellers)
Audit log: track who accessed or modified data at each tier

sections.title: vCISO Program Record System
sections.description: System of record for vCISO engagements. Ingests practitioner artifacts rather than replacing workflow — the vCISO keeps their tools and templates; the platform becomes the longitudinal client program record. Core principle: bring your own workflow.

items.text: Client Record & Program History Store: per-client record holding all uploaded artifacts organized by month and type (monthly report, assessment, TPRA, policy, tabletop, meeting notes). Builds a program timeline automatically from ingestion date and document type. No data entry beyond the upload itself.
items.notes: Foundational — all other vCISO program features depend on this store.

items.text: Monthly Report Ingestion & Signal Extraction: on upload of a monthly report (Word/PDF), extract key signals via AI — risk posture indicators, open action items, framework areas touched, deliverables referenced. Present extracted signals to the vCISO for a quick confirm/correct step before storing.
items.notes: Core AI intelligence layer. Turns unstructured document into structured program data without requiring the vCISO to change their report format.

items.text: Hours Input — Lightweight, Not a Timesheet: single input per month per client — hours consumed, hours budgeted, optional activity tag. No timesheets, no per-task logging. The vCISO loads the number however they track it; the tool stores the result.

Client Health Dashboard (practitioner-facing): portfolio view showing all clients at a glance — burn rate vs. retainer, last activity date, open action items count, months of program history. Surfaces clients burning hot or going dark before it becomes a problem.
items.notes: Built for the vCISO, not the client. Practitioner-facing only.

items.text: Client Portal — Program View (client-facing): thin read-only view for the client — program timeline, deliverables received, risk posture trend, open action items, document library. Derived entirely from ingested artifacts — no additional data entry to populate it. Answers 'what are we paying for?' before it gets asked.
items.notes: Build after ingestion layer (vciso1, vciso2) is stable and trusted. Phase 3 candidate.

sections.title: Risk Register — Core Structure & Columns
sections.description: POAM-driven risk register. PATCH_014 (session 21) built an 18-row auto-calculated model; PATCH_015 (session 22) replaced it with individual risk items driven from CIS POAM gaps. One risk_register row per POAM safeguard per org (stable key: org_id + safeguard_id). Manual risks (source=manual) support full CRUD. sync_cis_poam_to_risk_register() DB function upserts on every cisSavePoam() call. Status vocabulary: Open / In Progress / Accepted / Closed / Transferred.

items.text: Risk ID: auto-generated unique identifier per risk entry (e.g. RSK-0042)
items.notes: N/A in CIS-auto architecture — UUID pk is used. May revisit for manual risk entries in a future phase.

items.text: Risk Title: short descriptive name of the risk
items.notes: Covered by risk_control_categories.control_name (e.g. 'Account Management'). One row per CIS Control.

items.text: Risk Description: full narrative of what the risk is and how it arises
items.notes: risk_control_categories.threat_scenario provides the risk narrative. Shown in Accept modal.

items.text: Risk Category: dropdown (Operational / Technical / Compliance / Third-Party / Physical / Strategic)
items.notes: Not in current architecture — CIS control group is the category. Could add asset_type column to UI.

items.text: Affected Asset / System: what is exposed (server, app, process, data type)
items.notes: risk_subcontrols.asset_type carries this per safeguard (Devices/Network/Data/Users/Applications/N/A).

items.text: Threat Source: internal / external / natural / third-party
Likelihood: scored 1–5 (Rare / Unlikely / Possible / Likely / Almost Certain)
items.notes: Replaced by inherent_risk_score (1–4) pre-seeded per CIS control group. No separate likelihood field.

items.text: Impact: scored 1–5 (Negligible / Minor / Moderate / Major / Critical)
items.notes: Replaced by inherent_risk_rating (Critical/High/Medium/Low) pre-seeded per CIS control group.

items.text: Inherent Risk Score: auto-calculated Likelihood × Impact (1–25)
items.notes: risk_register.inherent_risk_score (1–4 scale) copied from risk_control_categories at row creation.

items.text: Current Controls: describe existing mitigations in place
items.notes: CIS safeguard answers (yes/no/partial) are the control evidence. No free-text control description field yet.

items.text: Control Effectiveness: rated Low / Medium / High
items.notes: Replaced by weighted pass rate from safeguard answers: yes=100%, partial=50%, no=0%.

items.text: Residual Risk Score: adjusted score after control effectiveness applied
items.notes: risk_register.residual_risk_rating (Critical/High/Medium/Low). Editable by user in Edit Notes modal (POAM rows) or Edit modal (manual rows). Not auto-calculated — requires practitioner judgement. PATCH_015.

items.text: Risk Treatment: dropdown (Accept / Mitigate / Transfer / Avoid)
items.notes: PATCH_015: risk_status = Open / In Progress / Accepted / Closed / Transferred. Accept via modal (accepted_by, rationale, review date) for manual risks. Transfer flows from POAM risk_decision='transfer'. Manual risks can be edited to any status. POAM-sourced statuses sync from POAM — not changeable in risk register.

items.text: Treatment Plan / Notes: free-text field for planned remediation actions
items.notes: risk_register.treatment_notes. Editable in Edit Notes modal (POAM rows) and Edit modal (manual rows). PATCH_015.

items.text: Risk Owner: person or role accountable for this risk
items.notes: risk_register.risk_owner. Present for all risk types, editable in Edit Notes (POAM) and Edit (manual) modals. PATCH_015.

items.text: Review Date: scheduled next review date
items.notes: risk_register.acceptance_review_date. Set at acceptance time, default 1 year. Shown in table row sub-line.

items.text: Date Identified: when the risk was first logged
items.notes: risk_register.created_at — set when first CIS assessment triggers initialize_risk_register.

items.text: Last Updated: timestamp of most recent edit
items.notes: risk_register.updated_at + last_calculated_at. Shown in module header.

items.text: Status: Open / In Remediation / Accepted / Closed
items.notes: PATCH_015: risk_status = Open / In Progress / Accepted / Closed / Transferred. Filter tabs in UI. Accepted = won't fix (formal risk acceptance). Closed = remediated. Transferred = cyber insurance or third-party.

items.text: Framework Mapping: link risk to CIS control / NIST CSF function / ISO domain
items.notes: risk_register.framework_id → risk_frameworks (CIS_V8). Abstraction layer ready for NIST CSF / NIST AI RMF.

items.text: Org Tier: tag risk to Child / Father / Grandfather level (for hierarchy rollup)
items.notes: risk_register.org_id → organisations. Hierarchy is derived from the org. Rollup view is a future phase item.

sections.title: Tabletop Program — Core Framework
sections.description: Scenario library, exercise builder, scheduling, and facilitator guide generation.

items.text: Tabletop exercise library: pre-built MITRE ATT&CK aligned scenarios (ransomware, BEC, insider, supply chain, DDoS, data breach)
Operational track: IT/security team with vCISO facilitator console
Executive track (C-suite/board)
Vendor/Third-Party track
Scenario builder: create custom exercises from scratch or clone/modify existing ones
Scenario metadata: industry relevance tags, estimated duration, difficulty, required participants
Map each scenario to NIST IR phases and MITRE ATT&CK tactics/techniques
Exercise scheduling: set date, time, participants, and facilitator per exercise
Recurring schedule support: annual, semi-annual, or quarterly cadence per track
Exercise status tracking: Planned / In Progress / Completed / Overdue
Facilitator guide: inject sequence, facilitator notes, timing cues, correct criticality per inject
Participant invite system: send exercise brief and pre-read materials ahead of session
Email delivery option for remote participants (notify by email instead of dashboard)

Scenario Library (platform-layer): pre-built scenarios by threat profile and vertical — ransomware, BEC/wire fraud, AiTM credential theft, supply chain compromise, regulatory audit surprise. Scenarios include timed injects, role mapping pre-populated from client onboarding data, and frequency tracking for compliance programs (HIPAA, CMMC, cyber insurance).

sections.title: Tabletop — Operational Track (IT / Security Team)
sections.description: Technical scenario track for IT and security teams with vCISO facilitator console.

items.text: Scenarios: ransomware via phishing (built), BEC wire fraud (built), active directory compromise, cloud misconfiguration, credential theft
Step 0 — TL Declaration: Technical Lead receives raw signal, assigns severity (P1–P4), recommends declare or monitor before IR plan activates
vCISO commentary card: exercise briefing shown at launch explaining TL declaration flow and participant roles
Three ingestion points: SOC alert, technician anomaly, PSA customer ticket
Role-filtered inject cards: each role sees situation-appropriate information per inject
Roles: Incident Commander (vCISO), Technical Lead, Communications Lead, Legal/Compliance, Executive Sponsor (assumed by ops participant)
Executive Sponsor role card: displayed at breach declaration gate explaining assumed-role mindset and responsibilities
Playbook alignment: map exercise steps to existing IR / DR playbooks
Gap identification: note where playbook breaks down or team is unsure during exercise
Tool availability check: confirm which tools/systems would be available during a real incident
Escalation path practice: comms test baked into role-specific injects
Real-time response log: each role logs actions and decisions per inject

sections.title: Tabletop — Executive Track (C-Suite / Board)
sections.description: Business-framed scenario track for executives and board members.

items.text: Scenarios: ransomware with ransom demand decision, regulatory breach notification, reputational crisis, M&A cyber due diligence failure, cyber insurance claim
Business impact framing: scenarios presented in revenue, reputation, and regulatory terms — not technical
Decision inject cards: executives presented with choices — pay/don't pay, notify/delay, shut down/continue operations
Legal & regulatory prompts: when does GDPR/PIPEDA breach notification clock start, who is the regulator
Board communication exercise: draft a stakeholder communication under simulated pressure
Insurance review prompt: what does the policy cover, what are the exclusions
Executive debrief template: document decisions made, rationale, and what would be done differently
Cyber risk appetite discussion: use exercise outcome to calibrate exec risk tolerance

sections.title: Tabletop — Vendor / Third-Party Track
sections.description: Scenario track focused on third-party and supply chain risk.

items.text: Scenarios: critical vendor ransomware impact, supply chain compromise (SolarWinds-style), vendor data breach exposing client data, vendor going dark during incident
Vendor notification drill: how and when does the vendor notify you, is it in the contract
Shared responsibility mapping: who owns what during a vendor-side incident
Vendor IR plan review: does the vendor have an IR plan, can you see it, does it meet your standards
Substitution/continuity exercise: if this vendor went offline for 72hrs, what is the fallback
Contractual gap identification: log SLA/notification gaps discovered during the exercise
Vendor scorecard update: findings from exercise feed back into vendor risk register

sections.title: Tabletop — After Action & Reporting
sections.description: Post-exercise documentation, action tracking, and compliance evidence.

items.text: After Action Report (AAR): auto-generated from facilitator notes, response logs, and criticality ratings captured during exercise
AAR sections: summary metrics, TL declaration accuracy, MITRE mapping revealed, criticality accuracy by role, full event timeline, breach declaration record, IR plan comparison
IR plan comparison — automated: upload ratified IR plan document and auto-compare against exercise event log
Action items log: capture owners, due dates, and priority for each identified gap
Action items linked to risk register: gaps auto-create or update risk entries
Action item tracking: open / in progress / closed with due date alerts
Exercise history: full log of all exercises run per org with AAR attached
items.notes: Session 18: js/ex_hub.js — Exercise Hub unified view combining Operational tabletop (from tabletop_sessions table via sb.tt.listCompletedForOrg) and AI Governance tabletop (from orgAssessments[id]['ai_tabletop']). Stat strip (total/op/ai/breach count), sortable table with date/track badge/scenario/facilitator/outcome/activity/View AAR. exHubViewOpAAR() and exHubViewAiAAR() navigate to respective modules with history pre-loaded. Operational tabletop history also added inline below the New Exercise card in ttRenderSetup(). Nav item ex_hub added to g_exercises group in config.js.

items.text: Trend view: which gaps recur across multiple exercises over time
Grandfather/Father visibility: view exercise completion status across Child orgs
Export AAR to PDF: branded, client-ready after action report (Anthropic API)
Export action items to Excel: same format as risk register for consistency
Compliance evidence: mark exercises as evidence for NIST / ISO / SOC 2 audit readiness

Vendor Breach Scenario Inject: post-TPRA, offer to generate a one-page tabletop scenario pre-populated from the assessment — data categories exposed, regulatory notification clock (jurisdiction already captured at intake), decision-maker identification, cyber insurance trigger, and DPA contractual rights. No manual prep required.

Findings-to-Remediation Loop: tabletop gaps (missing DPA, unknown notification timeline, no IR decision tree) output as structured action items in the same format as TPRA findings — feeding directly into the client's risk register and remediation roadmap. Closes the loop no competing platform currently closes.

sections.title: Tabletop — Multiplayer / Remote Participant Engine
sections.description: Jackbox-style session joining: facilitator generates a session code, participants join via link on any device, select their role, and receive role-filtered injects in real time. No accounts required for participants.

items.text: Session host: vCISO creates a session and receives a unique 6-character session code (e.g. CYBER4)
Join link: participants navigate to a URL and enter the session code to join — no account or login required
Role selection screen: participant sees available roles for the session, selects one, enters their name — role is locked once taken
Role capacity: each role can only be claimed by one participant — late joiners see remaining open roles only
Waiting room: participants see who has joined and which roles are filled while facilitator prepares to launch
Facilitator lobby view: see all connected participants, their roles, and connection status before launching
Role-filtered inject delivery: when facilitator releases an inject, each participant sees only their role-specific information on their device
Participant response input: each role submits their response and criticality rating from their own device
Facilitator sees all responses in real time: dashboard shows which roles have responded and which are pending per inject
Facilitator-only view: facilitator notes and correct criticality are never shown on participant screens
Breach declaration: IC and Exec Sponsor co-sign from their own devices — both must confirm before breach is logged
Session persistence: if a participant disconnects and rejoins with the same code and role, their session state is restored
Session expiry: sessions auto-close after exercise completion or after a configurable idle period (e.g. 4 hours)
AAR available to all participants post-exercise: shareable read-only link to the After Action Report
Mobile-responsive participant view: join and participate fully from a phone or tablet
